title.zh: 卷七十四 列傳第六十四 孝義下
title.raw: 卷七十四 列傳第六十四 孝義下 Volume 74 Biographies 64: Filial Acts 2

sentences.zh: 列傳第六十四孝義下

translations.literal: Biographies Sixty-Four, Filial Piety (Lower Part)
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 64: Filial Acts (Part 2)

sentences.zh: 滕曇恭陶季直沈崇傃荀匠吉翂甄恬趙拔扈韓懷明褚修張景仁陶子鏘成景雋李慶緒謝藺殷不害司馬暠張昭

translations.literal: Teng Yan'gong, Tao Jizhi, Shen Chongsu, Xun Jiang, Ji Yin, Zhen Tian, Zhao Ba, Hu Hanming, Chu Xiu, Zhang Jingren, Tao Zishao, Cheng Jingjun, Li Qingxu, Xie Lin, Yin Buhai, Sima Hao, Zhang Zhao
translations.idiomatic: Teng Yan'gong, Tao Jizhi, Shen Chongsu, Xun Jiang, Ji Yin, Zhen Tian, Zhao Ba, Hu Hanming, Chu Xiu, Zhang Jingren, Tao Zishao, Cheng Jingjun, Li Qingxu, Xie Lin, Yin Buhai, Sima Hao, and Zhang Zhao

sentences.zh: 時有徐普濟者，長沙臨湘人。

translations.literal: At that time there was one Xu Puji, a man of Linxiang in Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: At that time there was a man named Xu Puji, from Linxiang in Changsha.

sentences.zh: 居喪未葬，而鄰家火起，延及其舍。

translations.literal: While in mourning before burial, a neighbor's house caught fire, and it spread to his dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: He was still in mourning and had not yet buried the dead when a neighbor's house caught fire and the blaze spread to his home.

sentences.zh: 普濟號慟伏棺上，以身蔽火。

translations.literal: Puji wailed and lay prone on the coffin, using his body to shield it from the fire.
translations.idiomatic: Puji cried out in grief and threw himself on the coffin, shielding it with his own body.

sentences.zh: 鄰人往救之，焚炙已悶絕，累日方蘇。

translations.literal: Neighbors went to rescue him; he had already been scorched into unconsciousness, and only after many days did he revive.
translations.idiomatic: Neighbors rushed to pull him away, but he had already been burned into unconsciousness and did not come to for several days.

sentences.zh: 又有建康人張悌，家貧無以供養，以情告鄰富人。

translations.literal: There was also Zhang Ti of Jiankang, whose family was poor and unable to provide support; he explained his situation to a wealthy neighbor.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Zhang Ti of Jiankang, whose family was too poor to support their dependents; he appealed to a wealthy neighbor for help.

sentences.zh: 富人不與，不勝忿，遂結四人作劫，所得衣物，三劫持去，實無一錢入己。

translations.literal: The rich man would not give; unable to contain his anger, he then joined four others in robbery. Of the clothing obtained, the three companions took it away; not a single coin entered his own possession.
translations.idiomatic: When the rich man refused, Zhang Ti could not contain his anger and banded with four others to rob. His three accomplices took all the clothing; not a single coin went into his own pocket.

sentences.zh: 縣抵悌死罪。

translations.literal: The county charged Ti with a capital offense.
translations.idiomatic: The county sentenced Zhang Ti to death.

sentences.zh: 悌兄松訴稱：「與弟景是前母子，後母唯生悌，松長不能教誨，乞代悌死。

translations.literal: Ti's elder brother Song petitioned, saying: "My younger brother Jing and I are sons of the former wife; the stepmother bore only Ti. As the eldest, I could not instruct him properly—I beg to die in Ti's place.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ti's elder brother Song petitioned the court: "My brother Jing and I are sons of our father's first wife; our stepmother bore only Ti. As the eldest son I failed to guide him properly—I beg to die in his stead.

sentences.zh: 」景又曰：「松是嫡長，後母唯生悌。

translations.literal: " Jing also said: "Song is the legitimate eldest; the stepmother bore only Ti.
translations.idiomatic: " Jing added: "Song is the legitimate eldest son, and our stepmother bore only Ti.

sentences.zh: 若從法，母亦不全。

translations.literal: If the law is followed, the mother too will not remain whole.
translations.idiomatic: If the law is enforced, our mother will be left without a son as well.

sentences.zh: 」亦請代死。

translations.literal: " He too asked to die in another's place.
translations.idiomatic: " He too asked to die in Ti's place.

sentences.zh: 母又云：「悌應死，豈以弟罪枉及諸兄。

translations.literal: The mother also said: "Ti deserves death—how can a younger brother's crime wrongly involve all the elder brothers?
translations.idiomatic: Their mother said: "Ti deserves to die—how can a younger brother's crime drag all his elder brothers into it?

sentences.zh: 悌亦引分，乞全兩兄供養。

translations.literal: Ti also accepted his portion of blame and begged to spare both elder brothers for support.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ti accepted his guilt and begged that both elder brothers be spared so they could support the family.

sentences.zh: 」縣以上讞，帝以為孝義，特降死，後不得為例。

translations.literal: " The county reported the case upward; the emperor regarded it as filial righteousness and specially commuted the death sentence, with the stipulation that this should not serve as a precedent thereafter.
translations.idiomatic: " The county forwarded the case to the throne. The emperor judged it an act of filial devotion and specially commuted the death sentence, with the proviso that this should not set a precedent.

sentences.zh: 陶季直，丹陽秣陵人也。

translations.literal: Tao Jizhi was a man of Moling in Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Jizhi was a native of Moling in Danyang.

sentences.zh: 祖湣祖，宋廣州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Minzu was Governor of Guangzhou under Song.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Minzu had served as Governor of Guangzhou under the Liu Song.

sentences.zh: 父景仁，中散大夫。

translations.literal: His father Jingren was a Master of Leisurely Discourse.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jingren held the rank of Master of Leisurely Discourse.

sentences.zh: 季直早慧，湣祖甚愛異之，嘗以四函銀列置於前，令諸孫各取其一。

translations.literal: Jizhi was precocious; Minzu greatly favored and singled him out. Once he placed four boxes of silver in a row before them and had each grandson take one.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhi was precocious, and Minzu favored him greatly. Once the grandfather set out four boxes of silver and told each grandson to take one.

sentences.zh: 季直時年四歲，獨不取，曰：「若有賜，當先父伯，不應度及諸孫，故不取。

translations.literal: Jizhi was then four years old and alone did not take one, saying: "If there is a gift, it should go first to father and uncles; it should not pass down to the grandsons—therefore I do not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhi was only four and alone refused. He said, "If there is a gift, it should go to my father and uncles first, not to the grandsons—so I will not take one.

sentences.zh: 」湣祖益奇之。

translations.literal: " Minzu was all the more struck by his unusual quality.
translations.idiomatic: " Minzu was all the more astonished by the boy.

sentences.zh: 五歲喪母，哀若成人。

translations.literal: At five he lost his mother, grieving as if he were an adult.
translations.idiomatic: When he was five his mother died, and he mourned with the grief of a grown man.

sentences.zh: 初母未病，令於外染衣，卒後，家人始贖。

translations.literal: Earlier, before his mother fell ill, she had had clothing dyed outside; after her death the family only then redeemed it.
translations.idiomatic: Before his mother fell ill she had sent clothes out to be dyed; only after her death did the family redeem them.

sentences.zh: 季直抱之號慟，聞者莫不酸感。

translations.literal: Jizhi embraced the garments and wailed; all who heard were moved to bitter sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhi clutched the garments and wailed until all who heard him were moved to tears.

sentences.zh: 及長好學，澹于榮利，徵召不起，時人號曰聘君。

translations.literal: When grown he loved learning, was indifferent to glory and profit, and did not rise when summoned to office; people of the time called him the Reclusive Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew he devoted himself to learning, cared little for rank or profit, and declined every summons to office; contemporaries called him the Reclusive Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 後為望蔡令，以病免。

translations.literal: Later he became Magistrate of Wangcai and was dismissed on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Magistrate of Wangcai but resigned because of illness.

sentences.zh: 時劉彥節、袁粲以齊高帝權盛，將圖之。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Yanjie and Yuan Can, because the Qi founding emperor's power was great, were about to plot against him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liu Yanjie and Yuan Can, seeing how powerful the Qi founder had become, were plotting against him.

sentences.zh: 彥節素重季直，欲與謀。

translations.literal: Yanjie had always esteemed Jizhi and wished to conspire with him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjie had long held Jizhi in high regard and wanted him in on the plot.

sentences.zh: 季直以袁、劉儒者，必致顛殞，固辭不赴。

translations.literal: Jizhi considered Yuan and Liu men of learning who would surely bring ruin upon themselves, and firmly declined to go.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhi judged Yuan and Liu to be scholarly men who would only bring ruin on themselves, and firmly refused to join them.

sentences.zh: 俄而彥節等敗。

translations.literal: Before long Yanjie and the others were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Yanjie and his allies were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 齊初為尚書比部郎，時褚彥回為尚書令，素與季直善，頻以為司空司徒主簿，委以府事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qi he was Director in the Ministry of Revenue section of the Secretariat; at that time Chu Yanhui was Secretariat Director, had long been on good terms with Jizhi, repeatedly appointed him chief clerk to the Ministers of Works and Education, and entrusted him with bureau affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qi dynasty he became a director in the Secretariat's revenue section. Chu Yanhui, then Secretariat Director and an old friend, repeatedly named him chief clerk under the Ministers of Works and Education and entrusted him with bureau affairs.

sentences.zh: 彥回卒，尚書令王儉以彥回有至行，欲諡「文孝公」。

translations.literal: When Yanhui died, Secretariat Director Wang Jian, because Yanhui had utmost conduct, wished to posthumously title him Duke Wenxiao.
translations.idiomatic: After Yanhui died, Secretariat Director Wang Jian, citing his exemplary conduct, proposed the posthumous title Duke Wenxiao.

sentences.zh: 季直曰：「文孝是司馬道子諡，恐其人非具美，不如文簡。

translations.literal: Jizhi said: "Wenxiao was the posthumous title of Sima Daozi—I fear the man does not fully merit it; better Wenjian.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhi objected: "Wenxiao was Sima Daozi's posthumous title—that man hardly deserved full praise. Wenjian would be more fitting.

sentences.zh: 」儉從之。

translations.literal: " Jian followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: " Jian accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 季直又請為彥回立碑，始終營護，甚有吏節。

translations.literal: Jizhi also requested that a stele be erected for Yanhui and from first to last managed its care, showing great administrative integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhi also arranged for a stele to be raised for Yanhui and saw the project through from start to finish, displaying admirable administrative integrity.

sentences.zh: 再遷東莞太守，在郡號為清和。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to be Administrator of Dongguan; in the commandery he was known as pure and harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Administrator of Dongguan, where he earned a reputation for fair and gentle governance.

sentences.zh: 後為鎮西諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Later he was Staff Adviser to the Defender of the West.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as staff adviser to the Defender of the West.

sentences.zh: 齊武帝崩，明帝作相，誅鋤異己。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Qi died, Emperor Ming served as regent and executed those who differed from him.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu of Qi died, Emperor Ming took power as regent and purged his rivals.

sentences.zh: 季直不能阿意取容，明帝頗忌之，出為輔國長史、北海太守。

translations.literal: Jizhi could not curry favor by flattering; Emperor Ming was rather wary of him and sent him out as Chief Clerk to the Defender of the State and Administrator of Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhi would not flatter to please, and Emperor Ming grew wary of him, posting him out as chief clerk to the Defender of the State and Administrator of Beihai.

sentences.zh: 邊職上佐，素士罕為之者，或勸季直造門致謝，明帝留以為驃騎諮議參軍，兼尚書左丞，遷建安太守。

translations.literal: A senior aide on the frontier was a post that men of plain background rarely held; some urged Jizhi to call at the gate and offer thanks. Emperor Ming retained him as Staff Adviser to the Rapid Cavalry General, concurrently Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat, then transferred him to Administrator of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: A senior frontier post was seldom given to men of humble birth; some urged Jizhi to pay a courtesy call at court. Instead the emperor kept him on as staff adviser to the Rapid Cavalry General and concurrent Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat, then made him Administrator of Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 為政清靜，百姓便之。

translations.literal: His governance was pure and tranquil, and the common people found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was quiet and fair, and the people prospered under it.

sentences.zh: 梁台建，為給事黃門侍郎，常稱仕至二千石始願畢矣，無為久預人間事，乃辭疾還鄉里。

translations.literal: When the Liang regime was established, he became Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gate; he often said that reaching the two-thousand-bushel rank fulfilled his ambition, and that he should not long remain involved in worldly affairs—thereupon he pleaded illness and returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang regime was established he became Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gate. He had often said that reaching the two-thousand-bushel rank was all he had ever wanted, and that he should not linger in worldly affairs; he then pleaded illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 梁天監初，就拜太中大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Liang's Tianjian era he was appointed in his place as Grand Master of Palace Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianjian era he was appointed Grand Master of Palace Counsel at home.

sentences.zh: 武帝曰：「梁有天下，遂不見此人。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu said: "Liang has gained the realm, yet we do not see this man.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu remarked, "Now that Liang holds the realm, we still do not see this man at court.

sentences.zh: 」十年，卒於家。

translations.literal: " In the tenth year he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: " In the tenth year he died at home.

sentences.zh: 季直素清苦絕倫，又屏居十餘載，及死，家徒四壁，子孫無以殯斂，聞者莫不傷其志事云。

translations.literal: Jizhi had always been utterly abstemious and pure, and had lived in seclusion for more than ten years; when he died the house held only bare walls, and his descendants had no means for burial—all who heard grieved for his purpose and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhi had always lived in utter austerity and had kept to seclusion for more than a decade. When he died his house was bare to the walls and his descendants could not afford a proper burial; all who heard mourned both the man and his ideals.

sentences.zh: 沈崇傃字思整，吳興武康人也。

translations.literal: Shen Chongsu, style name Sizheng, was a man of Wukang in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Chongsu, courtesy name Sizheng, was a native of Wukang in Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 父懷明，宋兗州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Huaiming was Governor of Yanzhou under Song.
translations.idiomatic: His father Huaiming had been Governor of Yanzhou under the Liu Song.

sentences.zh: 崇傃六歲丁父憂，哭踴過禮。

translations.literal: Chongsu at six suffered his father's bereavement, weeping and stamping beyond the rites.
translations.idiomatic: At six Chongsu lost his father and mourned with weeping and stamping that exceeded the prescribed rites.

sentences.zh: 及長，事所生母至孝，家貧，常傭書以養。

translations.literal: When grown he served his birth mother with utmost filial piety; the family was poor, and he often copied documents for hire to support her.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew he served his birth mother with the utmost devotion. The family was poor, and he often copied documents for hire to support her.

sentences.zh: 天監二年，太守柳惲辟為主簿。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianjian the Administrator Liu Yun recruited him as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianjian the prefect Liu Yun appointed him chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 崇傃從惲到郡，還迎其母，未至而母卒。

translations.literal: Chongsu followed Yun to the commandery and returned to meet his mother, but before she arrived she died.
translations.idiomatic: Chongsu accompanied Yun to the prefecture and set out to bring his mother there, but she died before they could reunite.

sentences.zh: 崇傃以不及侍疾，將欲致死，水漿不入口，晝夜號哭，旬日殆將絕氣。

translations.literal: Chongsu, because he had not been able to attend her in illness, was about to die of grief; he took no food or drink, wailed day and night, and within ten days was nearly at his last breath.
translations.idiomatic: Grieving that he had not been there to nurse her, Chongsu nearly starved himself to death: he took no food or drink and wailed day and night until after ten days he was close to expiring.

sentences.zh: 兄弟謂曰：「殯葬未申，遽自毀滅，非全孝道也。

translations.literal: His brothers said to him: "Burial and funeral rites are not yet arranged—if you hasten to destroy yourself, you do not fulfill filial piety in full.
translations.idiomatic: His brothers told him, "The funeral has not yet been arranged—if you destroy yourself now you will not have fulfilled your filial duty.

sentences.zh: 」崇傃心悟，乃稍進食。

translations.literal: " Chongsu's heart understood, and he then gradually took food.
translations.idiomatic: " Chongsu took their words to heart and slowly began to eat again.

sentences.zh: 母權瘞，去家數里，哀至輒之瘞所，不避雨雪。

translations.literal: His mother was provisionally interred several li from home; whenever grief seized him he went to the burial place, not avoiding rain or snow.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was given a provisional burial several li from home. Whenever grief overwhelmed him he went to the grave, heedless of rain or snow.

sentences.zh: 每倚墳哀慟，飛鳥翔集。

translations.literal: Each time he leaned on the mound in bitter lament, birds would fly down and gather.
translations.idiomatic: Each time he leaned on the mound and wailed, birds would fly down and circle above him.

sentences.zh: 夜恒有猛獸來望之，有聲狀如歎息者。

translations.literal: At night fierce beasts constantly came to gaze at him, with sounds like sighing.
translations.idiomatic: At night wild beasts would come and watch him, making sounds like sighs.

sentences.zh: 家貧無以遷厝，乃行乞經年，始獲葬焉。

translations.literal: The family was poor and had no means to move the remains for proper burial; he then begged for a full year before he could obtain burial.
translations.idiomatic: Too poor to give her a proper burial, he begged for a full year before he could afford one.

sentences.zh: 既而廬於墓側，自以初行喪禮不備，復以葬後更行服三年。

translations.literal: Thereafter he built a mourning hut beside the tomb; considering that the initial mourning rites had been incomplete, after the burial he again observed mourning for three years.
translations.idiomatic: He then built a mourning hut beside the tomb. Judging that the first mourning had been incomplete, he observed another three years of mourning after the burial.

sentences.zh: 久食麥屑，不噉鹽酢，坐臥于單薦，因虛腫不能起。

translations.literal: For a long time he ate only wheat bran, took no salt or vinegar, and sat and lay on a single mat; from emaciation and swelling he could not rise.
translations.idiomatic: For a long time he ate only wheat bran and took no salt or vinegar, sitting and sleeping on a single mat until he swelled with edema and could not stand.

sentences.zh: 郡縣舉至孝。

translations.literal: The commandery and county recommended him for utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: The local authorities recommended him for supreme filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 梁武聞，即遣中書舍人慰勉之，乃詔令釋服，擢補太子洗馬，旌其門閭。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang heard, he immediately sent a Palace Secretariat Attendant to comfort and encourage him, then issued an edict ordering him to end mourning, promoted him to fill the post of Groom of the Heir Apparent, and honored his household gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu heard of it he sent a palace attendant to comfort him, then ordered him to end mourning, appointed him Groom of the Heir Apparent, and honored his household.

sentences.zh: 崇傃奉詔釋服，而涕泣如居喪。

translations.literal: Chongsu received the edict and ended mourning, yet wept as if still in bereavement.
translations.idiomatic: Chongsu obeyed the edict and ended mourning, but wept as if he were still in bereavement.

sentences.zh: 固辭不受官，乃除永寧令。

translations.literal: He firmly declined and did not accept office; he was then appointed Magistrate of Yongning.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined the appointment and was instead made Magistrate of Yongning.

sentences.zh: 自以祿不及養，哀思不自堪，未至縣，卒。

translations.literal: He considered that his salary had not reached his mother in time to support her; grief he could not bear—before reaching the county seat he died.
translations.idiomatic: He felt that his salary had come too late to support his mother, and grief overwhelmed him; he died before reaching the county seat.

sentences.zh: 荀匠字文師，潁陰人，晉太保勖九世孫也。

translations.literal: Xun Jiang, style name Wenshi, was a man of Yingyin, ninth-generation descendant of Jin's Grand Tutor Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Jiang, courtesy name Wenshi, was from Yingyin and a ninth-generation descendant of the Jin Grand Tutor Xun Xu.

sentences.zh: 祖瓊，年十五復父仇于成都巿，以孝聞。

translations.literal: His grandfather Qiong at fifteen avenged his father's death in the market at Chengdu and was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Qiong at fifteen avenged his father's death in the Chengdu market and won renown for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 宋元嘉末度淮，逢武陵王舉義，為元凶追兵所殺，贈員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanjia under Song he crossed the Huai; he encountered the Prince of Wuling raising righteous arms and was killed by the crown prince's pursuing troops, posthumously granted the title of Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Yuanjia era he crossed the Huai, encountered the Prince of Wuling's uprising, and was killed by the crown prince's pursuers; he was posthumously made Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 父法超，仕齊為安復令，卒官。

translations.literal: His father Fachao served Qi as Magistrate of Anfu and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fachao served the Qi as Magistrate of Anfu and died in office.

sentences.zh: 匠號慟氣絕，身體皆冷，至夜乃蘇。

translations.literal: Jiang wailed until his breath stopped and his whole body was cold; only at night did he revive.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang wailed until he stopped breathing and his whole body went cold; only at night did he come to.

sentences.zh: 既而奔喪，每宿江渚，商侶不忍聞其哭聲。

translations.literal: Thereafter he rushed to the funeral; each night he lodged on the river bank, and merchants could not bear to hear his weeping.
translations.idiomatic: He then hurried to the funeral, sleeping each night on the riverbank; merchants could not bear the sound of his weeping.

sentences.zh: 梁天監元年，其兄斐為郁林太守，征俚賊，為流矢所中，死於陣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Liang's Tianjian his elder brother Fei was Administrator of Yulin, campaigning against the Li bandits, and was struck by a stray arrow and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianjian his elder brother Fei, as Administrator of Yulin, was campaigning against Li bandits when a stray arrow struck him and he died on the field.

sentences.zh: 喪還，匠迎于豫章，望舟投水，傍人赴救，僅而得全。

translations.literal: When the coffin returned, Jiang met it at Yuzhang; seeing the boat he threw himself into the water; bystanders rushed to save him, and he barely survived.
translations.idiomatic: When the coffin returned Jiang met it at Yuzhang, saw the boat, and threw himself into the water; bystanders pulled him out barely alive.

sentences.zh: 及至，家貧不得時葬，居父憂並兄服，曆四年不出廬戶。

translations.literal: When he arrived home the family was poor and could not bury in timely fashion; he observed mourning for his father together with mourning for his brother, and for four years did not leave the mourning hut.
translations.idiomatic: At home the family was too poor for a timely burial. He mourned both father and brother together and did not leave the mourning hut for four years.

sentences.zh: 自括發不復櫛沐，發皆禿落，哭無時。

translations.literal: He gathered his hair himself and no longer combed or washed; his hair all fell out; he wept without regard to time.
translations.idiomatic: He twisted his own hair and stopped combing or washing until it all fell out; he wept without regard to day or night.

sentences.zh: 聲盡則系之以泣，目眥皆爛，形骸枯悴，皮骨裁連，雖家人不復識。

translations.literal: When his voice was exhausted he continued with sobbing; the corners of his eyes all rotted; his form withered and emaciated, skin and bone barely joined—even his family no longer recognized him.
translations.idiomatic: When his voice gave out he sobbed on; the corners of his eyes rotted away, his body wasted to skin and bone, and even his family could no longer recognize him.

sentences.zh: 郡縣以狀言，武帝詔遣中書舍人為其除服，擢為豫章王國左常侍。

translations.literal: The commandery and county reported the situation; Emperor Wu issued an edict sending a Palace Secretariat Attendant to release him from mourning and promoted him to Left Regular Attendant of the Kingdom of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: The local authorities reported his condition; Emperor Wu sent a palace attendant to release him from mourning and appointed him Left Regular Attendant in the Kingdom of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 匠雖即吉而毀悴逾甚，外祖孫謙誡之曰：「主上以孝臨天下，汝行過古人，故擢汝此職。

translations.literal: Although Jiang had returned to normal rites his devastation grew ever worse; his maternal grandfather Sun Qian admonished him, saying: "The sovereign rules the realm through filial piety; your conduct surpasses the ancients—therefore he promoted you to this post.
translations.idiomatic: Though Jiang had ended mourning his grief only deepened. His maternal grandfather Sun Qian admonished him: "The emperor rules the realm through filial example; your conduct surpasses the ancients, which is why he gave you this post.

sentences.zh: 非唯君父之命難拒，故亦揚名後世，所顯豈獨汝身哉。

translations.literal: It is not only that the lord and father's command is hard to refuse—thus too will your name be spread in later ages; what is displayed is not yours alone.
translations.idiomatic: It is not only that a ruler's command is hard to refuse—you will also win renown for generations. The glory shown is not yours alone.

sentences.zh: 」匠乃拜，竟以毀卒。

translations.literal: " Jiang then bowed in acceptance, but in the end died from devastation of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: " Jiang accepted the post, but in the end died of grief.

sentences.zh: 吉翂字彥霄，馮翊蓮勺人也。

translations.literal: Ji Yin, style name Yanxiao, was a man of Lianshao in Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Yin, courtesy name Yanxiao, was from Lianshao in Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 家居襄陽。

translations.literal: His family resided at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: His family lived at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 翂幼有孝性，年十一遭所生母憂，水漿不入口，殆將滅性，親黨異之。

translations.literal: Yin from youth had a filial nature; at eleven he suffered bereavement for his birth mother, took no food or drink, nearly perishing, and kin and friends marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was filial from childhood. At eleven he lost his birth mother, took no food or drink, and nearly died of grief; relatives and neighbors were astonished.

sentences.zh: 梁天監初，父為吳興原鄉令，為吏所誣，逮詣廷尉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Liang's Tianjian his father was Magistrate of Yuanxiang in Wuxing, was slandered by clerks, and was seized and sent to the Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianjian era his father served as Magistrate of Yuanxiang in Wuxing and was framed by subordinates; he was arrested and sent to the Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 翂年十五，號泣衢路，祈請公卿，行人見者皆為隕涕。

translations.literal: Yin was fifteen, wailing on the public roads, praying and pleading with dukes and ministers; passersby who saw him all shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was fifteen. He wailed in the streets and begged every minister he met; passersby wept at the sight.

sentences.zh: 其父理雖清白，而恥為吏訊，乃虛自引咎，罪當大辟。

translations.literal: Though his father's case was in principle innocent, he was ashamed to be examined by clerks and falsely took blame upon himself; the crime warranted execution.
translations.idiomatic: Though his father was innocent in fact, he was ashamed to be interrogated by petty officials and falsely confessed guilt, for which the penalty was death.

sentences.zh: 翂乃撾登聞鼓，乞代父命。

translations.literal: Yin then struck the Petition Drum at the palace gate and begged to die in his father's place.
translations.idiomatic: Yin then beat the Petition Drum at the palace gate and begged to die in his father's place.

sentences.zh: 武帝異之，尚以其童幼，疑受教於人，敕廷尉蔡法度嚴加脅誘，取其款實。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu was struck by this, yet because he was still young and childish suspected he had been taught by someone; he ordered Minister of Justice Cai Fadu to threaten and coax him severely and obtain a full confession of the facts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was moved but, because Yin was so young, suspected someone had put him up to it. He ordered Minister of Justice Cai Fadu to threaten and coax him until the truth came out.

sentences.zh: 法度乃還寺，盛陳徽纆，厲色問曰：「爾求代父死，敕已相許，便應伏法；

translations.literal: Fadu then returned to the tribunal, displayed fetters and chains in profusion, and with stern countenance asked: "You sought to die in your father's place—the edict has already granted it; you should submit to the law;
translations.idiomatic: Fadu returned to the tribunal, displayed chains and fetters, and demanded sternly: "You asked to die for your father—the edict has granted it, so you should submit to execution;

sentences.zh: 然刀鋸至劇，審能死不？

translations.literal: yet blade and saw are exceedingly harsh—can you truly die?
translations.idiomatic: but the blade and saw are cruel—can you truly face death?

sentences.zh: 且爾童孺，志不及此，必為人所教，姓名是誰？

translations.literal: Moreover you are a child—your will does not reach this; you must have been taught by someone—what is his name?
translations.idiomatic: Besides, you are a child—your mind cannot have reached this on its own. Someone must have taught you—what is his name?

sentences.zh: 若有悔異，亦相聽許。

translations.literal: If you have regret or change of mind, that too will be permitted.
translations.idiomatic: If you have changed your mind, you may say so and be heard.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「囚雖蒙弱，豈不知死可畏憚；

translations.literal: " He replied: "Though the prisoner is young and weak, how could he not know that death is to be feared;
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "Though I am young and weak, do I not know that death is to be feared?

sentences.zh: 顧諸弟幼藐，唯囚為長，不忍見父極刑，自延視息，所以內斷胸臆，上幹萬乘。

translations.literal: but considering that my younger brothers are young and small, only the prisoner is eldest—I cannot bear to see my father suffer extreme punishment and prolong my own breath; therefore I severed my heart within and appealed above to the ten-thousand-fold ruler.
translations.idiomatic: But my younger brothers are small and I alone am the eldest. I could not bear to see my father face execution while I drew breath, so I steeled my heart and appealed to the throne.

sentences.zh: 今欲殉身不測，委骨泉壤，此非細故，奈何受人教邪。

translations.literal: Now I wish to offer my body to the unknown and leave my bones in the springs and earth—this is no small matter; how could I accept instruction from another?
translations.idiomatic: Now I mean to give my life and leave my bones in the earth—this is no small thing. How could I have been taught by another?

sentences.zh: 」法度知不可屈撓，乃更和顏誘語之，曰：「主上知尊侯無罪，行當釋亮。

translations.literal: " Fadu knew he could not be bent or broken and then with gentler face coaxed him, saying: "The sovereign knows that your honored father is innocent and will soon release and clear him.
translations.idiomatic: " Seeing he could not be broken, Fadu softened his tone and said, "The emperor knows your father is innocent and will soon release him.

sentences.zh: 觀君神儀明秀，足稱佳童，今若轉辭，幸父子同濟，奚以此妙年苦求湯鑊。

translations.literal: Observing your bright and refined bearing, you fully deserve to be called a fine youth—if you now change your words, father and son may fortunately be saved together; why with this tender age bitterly seek the boiling cauldron?
translations.idiomatic: You are bright and handsome, a fine young man. If you change your plea now, father and son may both be spared—why at such a tender age seek the cauldron and cleaver?

sentences.zh: 」翂曰：「凡鯤鮞螻蟻尚惜其生，況在人斯，豈願齏粉。

translations.literal: " Yin said: "All creatures, from great fish and minnows to ants, still cherish their lives—how much more among mankind; who would wish to be ground to powder?
translations.idiomatic: " Yin said, "Even fish and ants cherish life—how much more a human being. Who would wish to be ground to powder?

sentences.zh: 但父掛深劾，必正刑書，故思殞僕，冀延父命。

translations.literal: But my father bears grave impeachment and will surely face formal punishment under the law; therefore I think to surrender my life, hoping to prolong my father's life.
translations.idiomatic: But my father faces serious charges and will surely be sentenced under the law, so I mean to give my life in the hope of prolonging his.

sentences.zh: 」翂初見囚，獄掾依法備加桎梏，法度矜之，命脫其二械，更令著一小者。

translations.literal: " When Yin was first imprisoned, the prison clerk, according to law, fully applied shackles and cangue. Fadu took pity on him, ordered two of his restraints removed, and had him wear only a smaller one.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin was first imprisoned, the jail clerk fully shackled him according to law. Fadu took pity on him, ordered two of the restraints removed, and had him wear a lighter one.

sentences.zh: 翂弗聽，曰：「翂求代父死，死囚豈可減乎。

translations.literal: Yin would not agree, saying: "Yin seeks to die in his father's place—how can restraints be lessened for a condemned prisoner?
translations.idiomatic: Yin refused, saying, "I ask to die in my father's place. How can shackles be loosened for a man awaiting execution?"

sentences.zh: 」竟不脫械。

translations.literal: " In the end he did not remove the restraints.
translations.idiomatic: He never removed the shackles.

sentences.zh: 法度以聞，帝乃宥其父。

translations.literal: Fadu reported it to the emperor, and the emperor then pardoned his father.
translations.idiomatic: Fadu reported the matter to the emperor, who then pardoned Yin's father.

sentences.zh: 丹陽尹王志求其在廷尉故事，並請鄉居，欲於歲首舉充純孝。

translations.literal: The Danyang Magistrate Wang Zhi sought his case records at the Court of Judicature and Review, and also requested his local residence records, intending to nominate him at the year's start as an exemplar of pure filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Danyang Magistrate Wang Zhi looked up his records at the Court of Judicature and Review and requested his village file, intending to nominate him at the New Year as an exemplar of pure filial piety.

sentences.zh: 翂曰：「異哉王尹，何量翂之薄，夫父辱子死，斯道固然，若翂有靦面目，當其此舉，則是因父買名，一何甚辱。

translations.literal: Yin said: "How strange, Magistrate Wang—why do you measure Yin so lightly? When a father's disgrace is answered by a son's death, that principle is only right; but if Yin had the face to undertake this act and still accept your proposal, then he would be buying a name through his father—how utterly shameful."
translations.idiomatic: Yin said, "How strange of you, Magistrate. Why do you think so little of me? When a father is disgraced and a son dies for him, that is only right—but if I had the nerve to do this and then accept your nomination, I would be trading on my father's shame for fame. What could be more humiliating?"

sentences.zh: 」拒之而止。

translations.literal: " He refused and put a stop to it.
translations.idiomatic: He refused, and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 年十七，應辟為本州主簿，出監萬年縣。

translations.literal: At seventeen he was summoned and appointed chief clerk of his province, and went out to supervise Wannian County.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen he was summoned to serve as chief clerk of his province and was sent to oversee Wannian County.

sentences.zh: 攝官期月，風化大行。

translations.literal: Acting in office for one month, customs and education were broadly carried out.
translations.idiomatic: In a single month as acting magistrate, he greatly improved local customs.

sentences.zh: 自雍還郢，湘州刺史柳忱復召為主簿。

translations.literal: Returning from Yong to Ying, the Xiangzhou Inspector Liu Chen again summoned him as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned from Yong to the capital at Ying, Xiangzhou Inspector Liu Chen again appointed him chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 後秣陵鄉人裴儉、丹陽尹丞臧盾、揚州中正張仄連名薦翂，以為孝行純至，明通易、老。

translations.literal: Later fellow townsman Pei Jian of Moling, Danyang Assistant Magistrate Zang Dun, and Yangzhou Rectifier Zhang Ze jointly recommended Yin, judging his filial conduct utterly pure and his mastery clear in the Changes and Laozi.
translations.idiomatic: Later his fellow townsman Pei Jian of Moling, Danyang Assistant Magistrate Zang Dun, and Yangzhou Rectifier Zhang Ze jointly recommended Yin, citing his utterly pure filial conduct and his mastery of the Book of Changes and the Laozi.

sentences.zh: 敕付太常旌舉。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Ministry of Rites to commend and nominate him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the Ministry of Rites to commend and nominate him.

sentences.zh: 初，翂以父陷罪，因成悸疾，後因發而卒。

translations.literal: Initially, because his father fell into crime, Yin developed a palpitating illness, and later died when it flared up.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the shock of his father's conviction had left Yin with a heart condition; he later died when it recurred.

sentences.zh: 甄恬字彥約，中山無極人也，世居江陵。

translations.literal: Zhen Tian, style name Yanyue, was a man of Wuji in Zhongshan; his family had long resided in Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen Tian, courtesy name Yanyue, was from Wuji in Zhongshan; his family had lived in Jiangling for generations.

sentences.zh: 數歲喪父，哀感有若成人。

translations.literal: He lost his father at several years of age, and his grief and feeling were like those of an adult.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father while still a small child, yet mourned as a grown man would.

sentences.zh: 家人矜其小，以肉汁和飯飼之，恬不肯食。

translations.literal: His family, pitying his youth, fed him rice mixed with meat broth; Tian would not eat.
translations.idiomatic: His family, pitying his tender age, tried to feed him rice mixed with meat broth, but Tian refused.

sentences.zh: 年八歲，嘗問其母，恨生不識父，遂悲泣累日。

translations.literal: At eight years he once asked his mother, regretting that he had been born without knowing his father, and then grieved and wept for many days.
translations.idiomatic: At eight he once told his mother how much he regretted never having known his father, and wept for days.

sentences.zh: 忽若有見，言形貌則其父也，時以為孝感。

translations.literal: Suddenly it was as if he saw someone—speaking of appearance, it was his father—and at the time people took it as filial feeling moving Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly he seemed to see someone who looked exactly like his father; people at the time took it as a sign that his filial devotion had moved Heaven.

sentences.zh: 家貧養母，常得珍羞。

translations.literal: Though the family was poor in supporting his mother, he always obtained delicacies.
translations.idiomatic: Though the family was poor, he always managed to provide his mother with delicacies.

sentences.zh: 及居喪，廬於墓側，恒有鳥玄黃雜色集於廬樹，恬哭則鳴，哭止則止。

translations.literal: When he dwelt in mourning, he built a hut beside the tomb; constantly there were birds of mixed dark and yellow hues gathering on the hut's trees—when Tian wept they cried, when his weeping stopped they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning he built a hut beside the tomb. Birds of mixed black and yellow constantly gathered in the trees above it—they cried when Tian wept and fell silent when he stopped.

sentences.zh: 又有白鳩白雀棲宿其廬。

translations.literal: Moreover white doves and white sparrows roosted and slept at his hut.
translations.idiomatic: White doves and white sparrows also came to roost at his mourning hut.

sentences.zh: 州將始興王憺表其行狀，詔旌表門閭，加以爵位。

translations.literal: The provincial commander, Prince Dan of Shixing, memorialized his conduct; an edict commended his household gate and lane, and conferred noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Dan of Shixing, the provincial commander, memorialized his conduct; the emperor ordered his gate to be honored and granted him a title of nobility.

sentences.zh: 恬官至安南行參軍。

translations.literal: Tian reached office as acting staff officer of Annan.
translations.idiomatic: Tian rose to the rank of acting staff officer of Annan.

sentences.zh: 趙拔扈，新城人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Bahu was a man of Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Bahu was from Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 兄震動富於財，太守樊文茂求之不已，震動怒曰：「無厭將及我。

translations.literal: His elder brother Zhendong was wealthy in property; the prefect Fan Wenmao demanded from him without cease. Zhendong angrily said: "This insatiability will soon reach me."
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Zhendong was wealthy. Prefect Fan Wenmao kept demanding money from him until Zhendong exploded: "Your greed will come for me next!"

sentences.zh: 」文茂聞其語，聚其族誅之。

translations.literal: " Wenmao heard his words, gathered his clan, and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Wenmao heard this, gathered his kinsmen, and had Zhendong killed.

sentences.zh: 拔扈走免，亡命聚黨，至社樹祝曰：「文茂殺拔扈兄，今欲報之，若事克，斫樹處更生，不克即死。

translations.literal: Bahu escaped and fled, became an outlaw and gathered followers; arriving at the shrine tree he prayed: "Wenmao killed Bahu's elder brother—now I wish to take revenge. If the matter succeeds, where the tree is cut new growth will appear; if not, then death."
translations.idiomatic: Bahu escaped, became an outlaw, and gathered a band of followers. At the village shrine tree he vowed: "Fan Wenmao killed my brother—if I succeed in revenge, new shoots will spring from where this tree is cut; if I fail, I shall die."

sentences.zh: 」三宿三枿生十丈餘，人間傳以為神，附者十餘萬。

translations.literal: " After three nights three shoots grew more than ten zhang; among the people it was spread as miraculous, and those who joined exceeded a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Within three nights three new shoots sprouted more than thirty feet tall. Rumor spread that this was divine, and more than a hundred thousand men rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 既殺文茂，轉攻傍邑。

translations.literal: Having killed Wenmao, he turned to attack neighboring districts.
translations.idiomatic: After killing Fan Wenmao, he turned to attack neighboring districts.

sentences.zh: 將至成都，十餘日戰敗，退保新城求降。

translations.literal: About to reach Chengdu, after more than ten days he was defeated in battle, withdrew and held Xincheng, and sought surrender.
translations.idiomatic: As he approached Chengdu, he was defeated after ten days of fighting, retreated to Xincheng, and sued for surrender.

sentences.zh: 文茂，黎州刺史文熾弟，襄陽人也。

translations.literal: Wenmao was the younger brother of Wenchi, Inspector of Lizhou, a man of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Wenmao was the younger brother of Lizhou Inspector Fan Wenchi and was himself from Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 韓懷明，上黨人也。

translations.literal: Han Huaiming was a man of Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: Han Huaiming was from Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 客居荊州。

translations.literal: He lived as a guest in Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His family had settled in Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 十歲，母患屍疰，每發輒危殆。

translations.literal: At ten years his mother suffered from corpse-malaria; each attack was immediately perilous.
translations.idiomatic: At ten his mother suffered from a chronic wasting illness; each attack brought her to the brink of death.

sentences.zh: 懷明夜於星下稽顙祈禱，時寒甚切，忽聞香氣，空中有人曰：「童子母須臾永差，無勞自苦。

translations.literal: Huaiming at night under the stars kowtowed and prayed; the cold was then extremely keen, when suddenly he smelled fragrance, and someone in the air said: "Young lad, your mother's illness will shortly be forever cured—do not toil to torment yourself."
translations.idiomatic: One freezing night Huaiming kowtowed under the stars and prayed. Suddenly he smelled incense, and a voice in the air said, "Your mother's illness will soon be cured for good. Do not torment yourself any longer."

sentences.zh: 」未曉而母平復，鄉里以此異之。

translations.literal: " Before dawn his mother recovered completely; the village took this as marvelously strange.
translations.idiomatic: Before dawn his mother had fully recovered; people in the village regarded it as a miracle.

sentences.zh: 十五喪父，幾至滅性，負土成墳，賻助無所受。

translations.literal: At fifteen he lost his father, almost to the point of destroying his nature; he carried earth and made the mound, and accepted none of the funeral gifts and aid.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he lost his father and nearly grieved himself to death. He piled the grave mound with his own hands and refused all funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 免喪，與鄉人郭麻俱師南陽劉虯。

translations.literal: When mourning was ended, together with fellow townsman Guo Ma he took as teacher Liu Qiu of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning ended he and a fellow townsman, Guo Ma, studied under Liu Qiu of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 虯嘗一日廢講，獨居涕泣，懷明竊問虯家人，答云是外祖亡日。

translations.literal: Qiu once on one day suspended lecturing, lived alone weeping; Huaiming secretly asked Qiu's family, and they answered that it was the anniversary of his maternal grandfather's death.
translations.idiomatic: One day Liu Qiu canceled his lecture and sat alone weeping. Huaiming quietly asked Liu's household and learned it was the anniversary of his maternal grandfather's death.

sentences.zh: 時虯母亦已亡矣，懷明聞之，即日罷學，還家就養。

translations.literal: At that time Qiu's mother was also already dead; when Huaiming heard this, that very day he ended his studies and returned home to support his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Liu's own mother was also dead. When Huaiming heard this, he quit his studies that same day and went home to care for his mother.

sentences.zh: 虯歎曰：「韓生無丘吾之恨矣。

translations.literal: Qiu sighed and said: "Student Han has none of Qiu Wu's regret."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qiu sighed and said, "Han will not die with the regret of Qiu Wu."

sentences.zh: 」家貧，肆力以供甘脆，嬉怡膝下，朝夕不離母側。

translations.literal: " His family was poor; he applied his strength to supply tasty and tender foods, bringing joy beneath her knees, morning and evening not leaving his mother's side.
translations.idiomatic: The family was poor, so he worked with his hands to provide fine foods and kept his mother company day and night, never leaving her side.

sentences.zh: 母年九十，以壽終。

translations.literal: His mother reached ninety years and died of old age.
translations.idiomatic: His mother lived to ninety and died a natural death.

sentences.zh: 懷明水漿不入口一旬，號哭不絕聲。

translations.literal: Huaiming for ten days did not take water or broth into his mouth, wailing without cease.
translations.idiomatic: For ten days Huaiming took no food or drink and wailed without stopping.

sentences.zh: 有雙白鳩巢其廬上，字乳馴狎，若家禽焉，服釋乃去。

translations.literal: A pair of white doves nested on his hut; nurturing their young they were tame and familiar, like domestic fowl; when mourning dress was ended they departed.
translations.idiomatic: A pair of white doves nested on his mourning hut, rearing their chicks there as tamely as barnyard birds; they left only when his mourning ended.

sentences.zh: 及除喪，蔬食終身，衣衾無所改。

translations.literal: When mourning was ended, he ate vegetables for life, and his clothing and bedding were unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he ate only vegetables for the rest of his life and never changed his clothes or bedding.

sentences.zh: 梁天監初，刺史始興王憺表言之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Liang Tianjian, the Inspector Prince Dan of Shixing memorialized about him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianjian era, Prince Dan of Shixing, as provincial inspector, memorialized about him.

sentences.zh: 州累辟不就，卒於家。

translations.literal: The province repeatedly summoned him but he did not accept; he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated summons from the province he declined; he died at home.

sentences.zh: 褚修，吳郡錢唐人也。

translations.literal: Chu Xiu was a man of Qiantang in Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Xiu was from Qiantang in Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 父仲都，善周易，為當時之冠。

translations.literal: His father Zhongdu was skilled in the Zhou Changes and was the foremost of the age.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhongdu was a master of the Book of Changes, unrivaled in his day.

sentences.zh: 梁天監中，歷位五經博士。

translations.literal: During Liang Tianjian he successively held the post of Erudite of the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianjian era he served as an Erudite of the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 修少傳父業，武陵王紀為揚州，引為宣惠參軍，兼限內記室。

translations.literal: Xiu in youth inherited his father's learning; when Prince Wuling Ji was in Yangzhou, he was invited as Aide of Xuanhui and concurrently Internal Recorder within the jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu studied his father's craft from youth. When Prince Ji of Wuling served as governor of Yangzhou, he appointed Xiu aide and personal secretary.

sentences.zh: 修性至孝，父喪毀瘠過禮，因患冷氣。

translations.literal: Xiu's nature was utmost filial; in his father's mourning he wasted and emaciated beyond the rites and thereby contracted a chills illness.
translations.idiomatic: Utterly filial by nature, Chu Xiu mourned his father so deeply that he grew gaunt beyond what the rites required and fell ill with a chronic chill.

sentences.zh: 及丁母憂，水漿不入口二十三日，每號慟輒嘔血，遂以毀卒。

translations.literal: When he entered mourning for his mother, for twenty-three days water and broth did not enter his mouth; each time he wailed and grieved he vomited blood, and thereby he died from excess of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he took no food or drink for twenty-three days; each fit of weeping brought up blood, and he died of grief.

sentences.zh: 張景仁，廣平人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Jingren was a man of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jingren was from Guangping.

sentences.zh: 父梁天監初為同縣韋法所殺，景仁時年八歲。

translations.literal: His father at the beginning of Liang Tianjian was killed by Wei Fa of the same county; Jingren was then eight years old.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianjian era his father was murdered by Wei Fa, a man from the same county; Jingren was eight at the time.

sentences.zh: 及長，志在復讎。

translations.literal: When grown, his intent was to take revenge.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up, he was determined to avenge his father.

sentences.zh: 普通七年，遇法于公田渚，手斬其首以祭父墓。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Putong, he encountered Fa at Gongtian Islet, with his own hand beheaded him to sacrifice at his father's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Putong he met Wei Fa at Gongtian Islet, cut off his head with his own hand, and offered it at his father's grave.

sentences.zh: 事竟，詣郡自縛，乞依刑法。

translations.literal: When the deed was done, he went to the commandery, bound himself, and begged to be treated according to the penal law.
translations.idiomatic: When it was done he went to the prefecture, bound himself, and asked to be punished according to law.

sentences.zh: 太守蔡天起上言于州，時簡文在鎮，乃下教褒美之，原其罪，下屬長蠲其一戶租調，以旌孝行。

translations.literal: Prefect Cai Tianqi reported upward to the province; at the time Jianwen was garrisoned there, and therefore issued an instruction commending and praising him, pardoning his crime, and ordering the subordinate district chief to remit one household's land tax and corvée, to honor his filial conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Cai Tianqi reported to the provincial office. Prince Jianwen was then in residence there; he issued a commendation, pardoned Zhang's crime, and ordered a district official to remit one household's taxes and corvée as a reward for his filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 又天監中，宣城宛陵女子與母同床眠，母為猛獸所取，女啼號隨挐猛獸，行數十里，獸毛盡落，獸乃置其母而去。

translations.literal: Also during Tianjian, a woman of Wanling in Xuancheng slept in the same bed as her mother; her mother was seized by a fierce beast. The girl wept and cried, followed and clutched the fierce beast, going several tens of li—the beast's hair all fell out, and the beast then set down her mother and left.
translations.idiomatic: Also during the Tianjian era, a woman of Wanling in Xuancheng was sleeping beside her mother when a wild beast seized her mother. The daughter chased it, screaming and clutching at the animal for miles until its fur fell out; the beast finally dropped her mother and fled.

sentences.zh: 女抱母猶有氣息，經時乃絕。

translations.literal: The girl embraced her mother, who still had breath; after some time she expired.
translations.idiomatic: The daughter held her mother, who still breathed; after a while she died.

sentences.zh: 鄉里言于郡縣，太守蕭琛表上，詔榜其門閭。

translations.literal: The village reported to the commandery and county; Prefect Xiao Chen memorialized upward, and an edict posted a placard at her gate and lane.
translations.idiomatic: The village reported the matter to the authorities; Prefect Xiao Chen memorialized the emperor, who ordered a plaque placed at her gate.

sentences.zh: 又霸城王整之姊嫁為衛敬瑜妻，年十六而敬瑜亡，父母舅姑咸欲嫁之，誓而不許，乃截耳置盤中為誓乃止。

translations.literal: Also the elder sister of Wang Zhenzhi, Prince of Bacheng, married and became the wife of Wei Jingyu; at sixteen Jingyu died. Parents and parents-in-law all wished to marry her off; she vowed and would not agree, then cut off her ear and placed it on a plate as oath, and only then did they stop.
translations.idiomatic: Also, the elder sister of Wang Zhenzhi, Prince of Bacheng, had married Wei Jingyu. When she was sixteen, Jingyu died. Both families wanted to remarry her, but she refused and swore an oath; she cut off her ear and placed it on a dish as proof, and only then did they relent.

sentences.zh: 遂手為亡婿種樹數百株，墓前柏樹忽成連理，一年許還復分散。

translations.literal: Thereupon with her own hand she planted several hundred trees for the deceased son-in-law; before the tomb the cypress trees suddenly formed joined trunks, and after about a year again separated.
translations.idiomatic: She personally planted hundreds of trees for her late husband. The cypresses before his tomb suddenly grew with intertwined trunks; after about a year they separated again.

sentences.zh: 女乃為詩曰：「墓前一株柏，根連復並枝。

translations.literal: The woman then composed a poem saying: "Before the tomb one cypress tree—roots joined again, branches merged."
translations.idiomatic: She wrote a poem: "Before the tomb a single cypress—roots joined, branches intertwined once more."

sentences.zh: 妾心能感木，頹城何足奇。

translations.literal: This handmaid's heart can move wood—how is collapsing a city wall worth calling strange?
translations.idiomatic: If my heart can move a tree, why should anyone marvel at a fortress brought down?"

sentences.zh: 」所住戶有燕巢，常雙飛來去，後忽孤飛。

translations.literal: " At the household where she lived there was a swallow's nest; they constantly flew in pairs coming and going, then suddenly one flew alone.
translations.idiomatic: At her home a pair of swallows had nested, flying back and forth together—then one day a single bird returned alone.

sentences.zh: 女感其偏棲，乃以縷系腳為志。

translations.literal: The woman, moved by its solitary roosting, then tied thread to its leg as a marker.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by the bird's lonely flight, she tied a thread around its leg as a mark.

sentences.zh: 後歲此燕果復更來，猶帶前縷。

translations.literal: Later in the year this swallow indeed came again, still bearing the former thread.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the swallow returned, still wearing the thread.

sentences.zh: 女復為詩曰：「昔年無偶去，今春猶獨歸。

translations.literal: The woman again composed a poem saying: "In former years it left without its mate; this spring it still returns alone."
translations.idiomatic: She wrote another poem: "Last year it left without its mate; this spring it returns alone again."

sentences.zh: 故人恩既重，不忍復雙飛。

translations.literal: The old person's kindness being already weighty, it cannot bear to fly paired again.
translations.idiomatic: The kindness it owes me is too deep—it will not pair and fly away again."

sentences.zh: 」雍州刺史西昌侯藻嘉其美節，乃起樓於門，題曰：「貞義衛婦之閭」。

translations.literal: " The Yongzhou Inspector Marquis Zao of Xichang admired her fine integrity, and therefore built a tower at her gate, inscribing it: "The Lane of the Chaste and Righteous Lady Wei."
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhou Inspector Marquis Zao of Xichang admired her virtue and built a pavilion at her gate, naming it "The Lane of the Chaste Lady Wei."

sentences.zh: 又表於台。

translations.literal: He also memorialized to the central government.
translations.idiomatic: He also reported the matter to the central government.

sentences.zh: 後有河東劉景昕事母孝謹，母常病癖三十餘年，一朝而瘳，鄉里以為景昕誠感。

translations.literal: Later there was Liu Jingxin of Hedong, who served his mother filially and respectfully; his mother constantly suffered from chronic abdominal illness for more than thirty years, and in one morning was cured—the village thought Jingxin's sincerity had moved Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Later, Liu Jingxin of Hedong served his mother with devoted filial piety. She had suffered from chronic abdominal illness for more than thirty years, then was cured in a single day; people in the village believed his sincerity had moved Heaven.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史湘東王繹辟為主簿。

translations.literal: The Jingzhou Inspector Prince Yi of Xiangdong summoned him as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhou Inspector Prince Yi of Xiangdong appointed him chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 陶子鏘字海育，丹陽秣陵人也。

translations.literal: Tao Zishao, style name Haiyu, was a man of Moling in Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Zishao, courtesy name Haiyu, was from Moling in Danyang.

sentences.zh: 父延，尚書比部郎。

translations.literal: His father Yan was a Gentleman of the Ministry of Revenue's Comparison Section.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yan was a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 兄尚，宋末為幸臣所怨，被系。

translations.literal: His elder brother Shang, at the end of Song was hated by a favorite minister and was imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Shang, at the end of the Song, had offended a favored courtier and was thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 子鏘公私緣訴，流血稽顙，行路嗟傷。

translations.literal: Zishao through public and private connections pleaded his case, blood flowing as he kowtowed; passersby sighed in grief.
translations.idiomatic: Zishao pleaded his brother's case through every channel he could find, kowtowing until his forehead bled; people on the road wept at the sight.

sentences.zh: 逢謝超宗下車相訪，回入縣詣建康令勞彥遠曰：「豈忍見人昆季如此而不留心。

translations.literal: He encountered Xie Chaozong alighting from his carriage to visit him; turning back he entered the county and went to Jiankang Magistrate Lao Yuanyuan, saying: "How can one bear to see a pair of brothers in such plight and not pay heed?"
translations.idiomatic: He met the scholar Xie Chaozong, who got down from his carriage to visit him. Xie then went to Jiankang Magistrate Lao Yuanyuan and said, "How can you see brothers in such straits and pay no attention?"

sentences.zh: 」勞感之，兄得釋。

translations.literal: " Lao was moved by this, and the elder brother was released.
translations.idiomatic: Lao was moved and released the elder brother.

sentences.zh: 母終，居喪盡禮。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he observed mourning with full rites.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he observed every mourning rite.

sentences.zh: 與範雲鄰，雲每聞其哭聲，必動容改色，欲相申薦。

translations.literal: He was neighbor to Fan Yun; whenever Yun heard his weeping, he always changed expression and color, wishing to recommend him to higher authorities.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yun lived next door; whenever he heard Zishao weeping he was visibly moved and wanted to recommend him for office.

sentences.zh: 會雲卒。

translations.literal: Just then Yun died.
translations.idiomatic: But before he could, Fan Yun died.

sentences.zh: 初，子鏘母嗜蓴，母沒後，恒以供奠。

translations.literal: At first, Zishao's mother loved water shield; after his mother perished, he always supplied it for offerings.
translations.idiomatic: His mother had loved water shield; after her death he always included it in her offerings.

sentences.zh: 梁武義師初至，此年冬營蓴不得，子鏘痛恨，慟哭而絕，久之乃蘇。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu's righteous army first arrived, that winter water shield could not be obtained; Zishao grieved bitterly, wailed and lost consciousness, and after long time revived.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu's army first arrived, that winter he could find no water shield for her offering. Zishao was stricken with grief, wept until he lost consciousness, and only slowly revived.

sentences.zh: 遂長斷蓴味。

translations.literal: Thereupon he permanently abstained from the taste of water shield.
translations.idiomatic: After that he never tasted water shield again.

sentences.zh: 成景雋字超，范陽人也。

translations.literal: Cheng Jingjun, style name Chao, was a man of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Jingjun, courtesy name Chao, was from Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 祖興，仕魏為五兵尚書。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xing served Wei as Minister of the Five Arms.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xing served the Northern Wei as Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 父安樂，淮陽太守。

translations.literal: His father Anle was Prefect of Huaiyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Anle was prefect of Huaiyang.

sentences.zh: 梁天監六年，常邕和殺安樂，以城內附。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Liang Tianjian, Chang Yonghe killed Anle and surrendered the city to submit to the Liang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianjian, Chang Yonghe killed Anle and surrendered the city to Liang.

sentences.zh: 景雋謀復讎，因殺魏宿預城主，以地南入。

translations.literal: Jingjun plotted revenge; accordingly he killed the Wei commander of Suyu city and brought the territory southward to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Jingjun plotted revenge, killed the Northern Wei commander of Suyu, and submitted the city to the south.

sentences.zh: 普通六年，邕和為鄱陽內史，景雋購人刺殺之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Putong, Yonghe was Internal Administrator of Poyang; Jingjun hired men to assassinate him.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Putong, Yonghe was magistrate of Poyang; Jingjun hired assassins to kill him.

sentences.zh: 未久，重購邕和家人鴆殺其子弟，噍類俱盡。

translations.literal: Not long after, he again hired men to poison Yonghe's family members and kill his sons and younger brothers—every mouth was utterly extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he hired men to poison Yonghe's kinsmen and kill his sons and brothers until not one was left.

sentences.zh: 武帝義之，每為屈法。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu admired his righteousness and each time bent the law for him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu admired his cause and repeatedly exempted him from punishment.

sentences.zh: 景雋家讎既雪，每思報效，後除北豫州刺史，侵魏，所向必推其智勇，時以比馬仙琕。

translations.literal: Jingjun's family vengeance already avenged, he always thought to repay with service; later he was appointed Inspector of Northern Yuzhou, invaded Wei, and wherever he went his wisdom and courage were relied upon—at the time he was compared to Ma Xianbi.
translations.idiomatic: Once his family's vengeance was complete, Jingjun sought to repay the emperor's favor. Later appointed governor of Northern Yuzhou, he raided Wei territory and was everywhere trusted for his wisdom and courage; people compared him to the general Ma Xianbi.

sentences.zh: 兼有政績見懷，北豫州吏人樹碑紀德。

translations.literal: He also had administrative achievements that people remembered fondly; the officials and people of Northern Yuzhou erected a stele recording his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: He was also loved for his achievements in office; officials and commoners of Northern Yuzhou erected a stele in his honor.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰忠烈云。

translations.literal: When he died, his posthumous title was Loyal and Heroic, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was given the posthumous title Loyal and Bold.

sentences.zh: 李慶緒字孝緒，廣漢郪人也。

translations.literal: Li Qingxu, courtesy name Xiaoxu, was a man of Qi in Guanghan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qingxu, courtesy name Xiaoxu, was from Qi in Guanghan.

sentences.zh: 父為人所害，慶緒九歲而孤，為兄所養，日夜號泣，志在復讎。

translations.literal: His father was killed by someone; Qingxu was orphaned at nine, was raised by his elder brother, wept day and night, and set his heart on taking revenge.
translations.idiomatic: His father had been murdered. Orphaned at nine, Qingxu was raised by his elder brother. Day and night he wept, his mind fixed on vengeance.

sentences.zh: 投州將陳顯達，仍于部伍白日手刃其仇，自縛歸罪，州將義而釋之。

translations.literal: He went to the provincial commander Chen Xianda, then in broad daylight within the ranks personally killed his enemy with his own hand, bound himself and returned to confess guilt; the provincial commander, deeming it righteous, released him.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the service of the provincial commander Chen Xianda. One day in broad daylight, while still among the troops, he killed his father's murderer with his own hand, then bound himself and surrendered to face punishment. The commander, judging the act righteous, set him free.

sentences.zh: 梁天監中，為東莞太守。

translations.literal: During the Tianjian era of Liang, he served as Administrator of Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Liang dynasty's Tianjian era he served as magistrate of Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂去職，廬於墓側，每慟嘔血數升。

translations.literal: Upon completing mourning for his mother he left office, built a hut beside the tomb, and each time he grieved he vomited several sheng of blood.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he resigned his post, built a mourning hut beside her tomb, and in his grief would vomit blood by the cupful.

sentences.zh: 後為巴郡太守，號良吏。

translations.literal: Later he became Administrator of Ba Commandery and was called a good official.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as magistrate of Ba Commandery and was known as an excellent administrator.

sentences.zh: 累遷衛尉，封安陸縣侯。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he reached Commandant of the Guard and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Anlu County.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to Commandant of the Guard and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Anlu.

sentences.zh: 益州三百年無復貴仕，慶緒承恩至此，便欲西歸。

translations.literal: For three hundred years Yizhou had produced no one of high office again; Qingxu, having received favor to this point, then wished to return west.
translations.idiomatic: For three hundred years no one from Yizhou had risen to such high rank. Having received the court's favor, Qingxu wished to return home to the west.

sentences.zh: 尋徙太子右衛率，未拜而卒。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Right Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard, but before he could assume the appointment he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Right Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard, but died before he could take up the post.

sentences.zh: 謝藺字希如，陳郡陽夏人，晉太傅安之八世孫也。

translations.literal: Xie Lin, courtesy name Xiru, was a man of Yangxia in Chen Commandery, eighth-generation descendant of Jin Grand Tutor Xie An.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Lin, courtesy name Xiru, was from Yangxia in Chen Commandery and an eighth-generation descendant of the Jin dynasty's Grand Tutor Xie An.

sentences.zh: 父經，北中郎諮議參軍。

translations.literal: His father Jing was Advisory Staff Officer to the General of the North.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jing served as advisory staff officer to the General of the North.

sentences.zh: 藺五歲時，父未食，乳媼欲令先飯，藺終不進。

translations.literal: When Lin was five, his father had not yet eaten; the wet nurse wanted him to eat first, but Lin would not touch food.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin was five, his father had not yet eaten. The wet nurse tried to make the boy eat first, but Lin refused to touch his food.

sentences.zh: 舅阮孝緒聞之，歎曰：「此兒在家則曾子之流，事君則藺生之匹。

translations.literal: His maternal uncle Ruan Xiaoxu heard of this and sighed, saying: "This child at home is of the sort of Zengzi; in serving his lord he would match Master Lin."
translations.idiomatic: His maternal uncle Ruan Xiaoxu heard of this and sighed. "At home this boy is another Zengzi," he said; "in serving his lord he would be the equal of Lin Xiangru."

sentences.zh: 」因名曰藺。

translations.literal: " Accordingly he was given the name Lin.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore given the name Lin.

sentences.zh: 稍授以經史，過目便能諷誦，孝緒每曰：「吾家陽元也。

translations.literal: Gradually he was taught the classics and histories; once he read them he could recite them from memory. Xiaoxu would often say: "The Yangyuan of our family."
translations.idiomatic: When he was taught the classics and histories, he could recite them after a single reading. Xiaoxu would often say, "He is the Yangyuan of our house."

sentences.zh: 」及丁父憂，晝夜號慟，毀瘠骨立。

translations.literal: " When he completed mourning for his father, he wailed day and night and wasted away until only bones remained standing.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he wailed day and night until he was wasted to skin and bone.

sentences.zh: 母阮氏常自守視譬抑之。

translations.literal: His mother, Lady Ruan, constantly watched over him herself and admonished him to restrain his grief.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Ruan, kept constant watch over him and urged him to restrain his grief.

sentences.zh: 服闋，吏部尚書蕭子顯嘉其至行，擢為王府法曹行參軍。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, Minister of the Civil Service Xiao Zixian admired his utmost conduct and promoted him to acting staff officer in the princely household's legal bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning period ended, Minister of the Civil Service Xiao Zixian, admiring his extraordinary filial devotion, appointed him acting legal staff officer in a princely household.

sentences.zh: 累遷外兵、記室參軍。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he became staff officer for external military affairs and recording secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to staff officer for external military affairs and recording secretary.

sentences.zh: 時甘露降士林館，藺獻頌，武帝嘉之。

translations.literal: At that time sweet dew fell at the Shilin Academy; Lin submitted a eulogy, and Emperor Wu praised it.
translations.idiomatic: When sweet dew fell at the Shilin Academy, Lin submitted a celebratory ode that Emperor Wu greatly admired.

sentences.zh: 有詔使制北兗州刺史蕭楷德政碑。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to compose a stele on the virtuous governance of Xiao Kai, Inspector of Northern Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict commissioned him to compose a stele commemorating the virtuous administration of Xiao Kai, governor of Northern Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 又奉詔令制宣城王奉述中庸頌。

translations.literal: He also received an edict ordering him to compose the Prince of Xuancheng's eulogy on expounding the Doctrine of the Mean.
translations.idiomatic: He was also ordered by imperial command to compose the Prince of Xuancheng's eulogy on the Doctrine of the Mean.

sentences.zh: 後為兼散騎常侍，使魏。

translations.literal: Later he served concurrently as Regular Attendant at the Secretariat and was sent as envoy to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served concurrently as Regular Attendant at the Secretariat and was sent on a mission to Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 會侯景入附，境上交兵，藺母既慮不得還，感氣而卒。

translations.literal: It happened that Hou Jing submitted and joined the south; fighting broke out along the borders. Lin's mother, already fearing he would not return, died of grief and distress.
translations.idiomatic: While he was away, Hou Jing defected to the Liang and fighting erupted along the frontier. Lin's mother, fearing her son would never return, died of grief.

sentences.zh: 及藺還，入境夜夢不祥，旦便投列馳歸。

translations.literal: When Lin returned, the night he entered the border he dreamed something inauspicious; at dawn he immediately left the convoy and galloped home.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin returned, he dreamed an ill omen the night he crossed the border. At dawn he broke from the envoy party and galloped home.

sentences.zh: 及至，號慟嘔血，氣絕久之，水漿不入口。

translations.literal: When he arrived, he wailed in grief and vomited blood; his breath stopped for a long while, and he would take neither water nor food.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived he wailed until he vomited blood and lost consciousness for a long time. He would take neither water nor food.

sentences.zh: 每哭，眼耳口鼻皆血流，經月餘日，因夜臨而卒。

translations.literal: Each time he wept, blood flowed from his eyes, ears, nose, and mouth; after more than a month, he died while keeping night vigil at the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Each time he wept, blood streamed from his eyes, ears, nose, and mouth. After more than a month he died during a night vigil at his mother's grave.

sentences.zh: 所制詩賦碑頌數十篇。

translations.literal: The poems, rhapsodies, steles, and eulogies he composed numbered several tens.
translations.idiomatic: He left behind several dozen poems, rhapsodies, stele inscriptions, and eulogies.

sentences.zh: 子貞。

translations.literal: His son was Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Zhen.

sentences.zh: 貞字元正，幼聰敏，有至性。

translations.literal: Zhen, courtesy name Yuanzheng, was clever and keen from childhood and possessed utmost nature.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen, courtesy name Yuanzheng, was clever from childhood and possessed an extraordinary depth of feeling.

sentences.zh: 祖母阮氏先苦風眩，每發，便一二日不能飲食。

translations.literal: His grandmother, Lady Ruan, had long suffered from dizziness; each time it flared she could not eat or drink for one or two days.
translations.idiomatic: His grandmother Lady Ruan had long suffered from vertigo. Whenever it struck, she could not eat or drink for a day or two.

sentences.zh: 貞時年七歲，祖母不食，貞亦不食，往往如此。

translations.literal: Zhen was then seven years old; when his grandmother did not eat, Zhen also did not eat—often it was thus.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was then seven. Whenever his grandmother could not eat, he would not eat either. It was often so.

sentences.zh: 母王氏授以論語、孝經，讀訖便誦。

translations.literal: His mother, Lady Wang, taught him the Analects and Classic of Filial Piety; once he finished reading he could recite them.
translations.idiomatic: His mother Lady Wang taught him the Analects and the Classic of Filial Piety. When he finished reading a passage he could recite it from memory.

sentences.zh: 八歲，嘗為春日閒居詩，從舅王筠奇之，謂所親曰：「至如'風定花猶落'，乃追步惠連矣。

translations.literal: At eight he once composed a poem, Spring Day in Seclusion; his mother's cousin Wang Yun marveled at it and said to those close to him: "As for the line 'the wind has stilled yet flowers still fall,' it follows in the steps of Huilian."
translations.idiomatic: At eight he composed a poem called Spring Day in Seclusion. His mother's cousin Wang Yun was astonished and told his intimates, "A line like 'the wind has stilled, yet the flowers still fall' already rivals Xie Huilian."

sentences.zh: 」年十三，尤善左氏春秋，工草隸蟲篆。

translations.literal: " At thirteen he was especially skilled in the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals and excelled at cursive script, clerical script, and seal script.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he was especially versed in the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals and skilled in cursive, clerical, and seal scripts.

sentences.zh: 十四，丁父艱，號頓於地，絕而復蘇者數矣。

translations.literal: At fourteen he completed mourning for his father; he cried out and collapsed to the ground, losing consciousness and reviving several times.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen, when his father died, he cried out and collapsed to the ground, losing consciousness and reviving several times.

sentences.zh: 初貞父藺以憂毀卒，家人賓客復憂貞，從父洽、族兄暠乃共請華嚴寺長爪禪師為貞說法。

translations.literal: Earlier Zhen's father Lin had died from grief and wasting; family and guests again feared for Zhen. His father's cousin Qia and his clansman elder brother Hao together invited the Long-Clawed Chan Master of Huayan Temple to preach the dharma to Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's father Lin had already died of grief. Family and guests now feared the same fate for Zhen. His father's cousin Qia and his clansman Hao together invited the Long-Clawed Chan Master of Huayan Temple to preach to him.

sentences.zh: 仍譬以母須侍養，不宜毀滅，乃少進饘粥。

translations.literal: They also admonished him that his mother required his care and he ought not destroy himself, whereupon he took a little thin gruel.
translations.idiomatic: They urged that his mother still needed his care and that he must not destroy himself. At last he took a little thin gruel.

sentences.zh: 及魏克江陵，入長安。

translations.literal: When Wei captured Jiangling, he entered Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Wei captured Jiangling, he was taken to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 暠逃難番禺，貞母出家于宣明寺。

translations.literal: Hao fled the turmoil to Panyu; Zhen's mother took the tonsure at Xuaming Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Hao fled the chaos to Panyu. Zhen's mother entered the clergy at Xuaming Temple.

sentences.zh: 及陳武帝受禪，暠還鄉里，供養貞母，將二十年。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Chen received the abdication, Hao returned to his native place and supported Zhen's mother for nearly twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Chen took the throne, Hao returned home and supported Zhen's mother for nearly twenty years.

sentences.zh: 初貞在周，嘗侍周武帝愛弟趙王招讀，招厚禮之。

translations.literal: Earlier, while Zhen was in Zhou, he once attended Prince Zhao, the beloved younger brother of Emperor Wu of Zhou, in his studies; Zhao treated him with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhen was in Northern Zhou, he served as reader to Prince Zhao, the beloved younger brother of Emperor Wu of Zhou, who treated him with great honor.

sentences.zh: 聞其獨處，必晝夜涕泣，私問知母在鄉，乃謂曰：「寡人若出居藩，當遣侍讀還家。

translations.literal: Hearing that when alone he wept day and night, he asked privately and learned his mother was in his homeland; he then said to him: "If I am sent out to govern a frontier fief, I shall dispatch my reader home."
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Zhen wept day and night when alone, the prince questioned him privately and learned that his mother was still in the south. He said, "If I am sent out to govern a frontier fief, I shall send you home."

sentences.zh: 」後數年，招果出，因辭，面奏請放貞還。

translations.literal: " Several years later Zhao was indeed sent out; taking leave, he personally memorialized requesting that Zhen be released to return.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later Prince Zhao was indeed sent to a frontier post. On taking leave he personally memorialized the throne, asking that Zhen be allowed to return home.

sentences.zh: 帝奇招仁愛，遣隨聘使杜子暉歸國。

translations.literal: The emperor marveled at Zhao's benevolence and sent him back to his country with the envoy Du Zihui.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired Prince Zhao's kindness and sent Zhen home with the envoy Du Zihui.

sentences.zh: 是歲陳太建五年也。

translations.literal: That year was the fifth year of Taojian of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: That was the fifth year of the Chen dynasty's Taojian era.

sentences.zh: 始自周還時，始興王叔陵為揚州刺史，引祠部侍郎阮卓為記室，辟貞為主簿。
