translations.literal: When he first returned from Zhou, Prince Shixing Shi Shuling was Inspector of Yangzhou; he brought in Vice Director of the Sacrificial Bureau Ruan Zhuo as recording secretary and recruited Zhen as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen first returned from Northern Zhou, Prince Shixing Shi Shuling was governor of Yangzhou. The prince appointed Ruan Zhuo of the Sacrificial Bureau as his recording secretary and recruited Zhen as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 尋遷府錄事參軍，領丹陽丞。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to recording secretary of the princely establishment and concurrently served as Assistant Magistrate of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to recording secretary of the princely establishment and concurrently served as assistant magistrate of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 貞知叔陵有異志，因與卓自疏于王。

translations.literal: Zhen knew Shuling harbored rebellious intent; accordingly he and Zhuo deliberately kept their distance from the prince.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen knew that Shuling harbored treasonous ambitions, and he and Zhuo deliberately kept their distance from the prince.

sentences.zh: 每有宴遊，輒以疾辭，未嘗參預，叔陵雅重之，弗之罪也。

translations.literal: Whenever there were feasts and outings he always pleaded illness and declined; he never took part. Shuling greatly esteemed him and did not blame him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the prince held feasts or outings, Zhen pleaded illness and never attended. Shuling held him in high regard and did not hold it against him.

sentences.zh: 及叔陵肆逆，唯貞與卓不坐。

translations.literal: When Shuling rose in rebellion, only Zhen and Zhuo were not implicated.
translations.idiomatic: When Shuling rebelled, only Zhen and Zhuo were not punished.

sentences.zh: 再遷南平王友，掌記室事。

translations.literal: Through a second promotion he became Companion to the Prince of Nanping and managed recording-secretary affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was next promoted to companion to the Prince of Nanping and put in charge of the prince's secretariat.

sentences.zh: 府長史汝南周確新除都官尚書，請貞為讓表，後主覽而奇之。

translations.literal: The princely establishment's chief administrator Zhou Que of Runan had just been appointed Minister of Justice; he asked Zhen to draft his memorial declining the appointment, and the Later Lord read it and marveled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Que of Runan, chief administrator of the princely establishment, had just been appointed Minister of Justice. He asked Zhen to draft the memorial declining the post. The Later Lord read it and was impressed.

sentences.zh: 及問知貞所作，因敕舍人施文慶曰：「謝貞在王家未有祿秩，可賜米百石。

translations.literal: When he asked and learned it was Zhen's work, he thereupon ordered Attendant Shi Wenqing: "Xie Zhen in the princely household has no salary or rank; grant him one hundred shi of grain."
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that Zhen had written it, he ordered Attendant Shi Wenqing, "Xie Zhen serves in a princely household without salary or rank. Grant him one hundred shi of grain."

sentences.zh: 」以母憂去職。

translations.literal: " He left office upon completing mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned when his mother died.

sentences.zh: 頃之，敕起還府，累啟固辭，敕不許。

translations.literal: Before long an edict recalled him to the princely establishment; he repeatedly memorialized firmly declining, but the edict would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict ordered him back to the princely establishment. He memorialized repeatedly to decline, but the order stood.

sentences.zh: 貞哀毀羸瘠，終不能之官舍。

translations.literal: Zhen, wasted by grief, was in the end unable to go to the official residence.
translations.idiomatic: Wasted by grief, Zhen was never able to return to his post.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書姚察與貞友善，及貞病篤，問以後事。

translations.literal: Minister of the Civil Service Yao Cha was on friendly terms with Zhen; when Zhen's illness grew grave, he asked about affairs after death.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of the Civil Service Yao Cha was Zhen's friend. When Zhen's illness grew grave, Yao asked about his final arrangements.

sentences.zh: 貞曰：「孤子釁禍所集，將隨灰壤，族子凱等粗自成立，己有疏付之，此固不足仰塵厚德。

translations.literal: Zhen said: "This orphaned son has gathered calamity upon himself and will soon follow the dust; my clansman's sons Kai and others have roughly established themselves—I have already entrusted a written instruction to them. This truly is not enough to burden your great virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Zhen said, "I am a man marked for misfortune and will soon be dust. My clansman's sons Kai and the others are more or less grown, and I have already left written instructions with them. That hardly warrants imposing on your great kindness."

sentences.zh: 弱兒年甫六歲，名靖，字依仁，情累所不能忘，敢以為托。

translations.literal: My weak child is just six years old, named Jing, courtesy name Yiren—the emotional tie I cannot forget; I venture to entrust him to you.
translations.idiomatic: But my little boy is only six. His name is Jing, courtesy name Yiren. He is the one tie of affection I cannot put aside, and I venture to ask you to look after him.

sentences.zh: 」是夜卒。

translations.literal: " That night he died.
translations.idiomatic: That night he died.

sentences.zh: 後主問察曰：「謝貞有何親屬？

translations.literal: The Later Lord asked Cha: "What relatives does Xie Zhen have?"
translations.idiomatic: The Later Lord asked Yao Cha, "What relatives does Xie Zhen have?"

sentences.zh: 「察以靖答，即敕長給衣糧。

translations.literal: " Cha answered with Jing, and an edict immediately ordered long-term provision of clothing and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Yao answered with the boy Jing, and the emperor immediately ordered that clothing and grain be provided for him indefinitely.

sentences.zh: 初貞之病，有遺疏告族子凱：「氣絕之後，若依僧家屍陀林法，是吾所願，正恐過為獨異。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhen was ill, he left a final written instruction telling his clansman's son Kai: "After my breath is cut off, if one follows the Buddhist charnel-ground method, that is my wish—but I fear it would be too singular."
translations.idiomatic: While Zhen was ill he left a final note to his clansman's son Kai: "After I die, burial in a Buddhist charnel ground would be my wish, but I fear that would be too unusual."

sentences.zh: 可用薄板周身，載以露車，覆以草席，坎山次而埋之。

translations.literal: One may use thin boards all around the body, carry it on an open cart, cover it with a straw mat, and bury it in a hollow beside the hill.
translations.idiomatic: Wrap the body in thin boards, carry it on an open cart covered with a straw mat, and bury it in a hollow beside a hill.

sentences.zh: 又靖年尚小，未閱人事，但可三月施小床，設香水，盡卿兄弟相厚之情。

translations.literal: Moreover Jing is still young and has not yet seen the ways of the world; you need only set up a small bed for three months and place incense water, fulfilling the deep affection among you brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Jing is still young and knows nothing of the world. For three months you may set up a small mourning couch and burn incense—that is enough to show the affection between you brothers.

sentences.zh: 即除之，無益之事，勿為也。」

translations.literal: Then remove it; do not do things without benefit."
translations.idiomatic: Then put it away. Do nothing more that serves no purpose."

sentences.zh: 殷不害字長卿，陳郡長平人也。

translations.literal: Yin Buhai, courtesy name Changqing, was a man of Changping in Chen Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Buhai, courtesy name Changqing, was from Changping in Chen Commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖汪，齊豫章王行參軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Wang was acting staff officer to the Prince of Yuzhang of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Wang served as acting staff officer to the Prince of Yuzhang under Qi.

sentences.zh: 父高明，梁尚書中兵郎。

translations.literal: His father Gaoming was Central Military Officer in the Ministry of Works under Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gaoming served as Central Military Officer in the Ministry of Works under Liang.

sentences.zh: 不害性至孝，居父憂過禮，由是少知名。

translations.literal: Buhai's nature was utmost filial; in mourning for his father he exceeded the rites, and thereby became known while still young.
translations.idiomatic: Buhai was profoundly filial. In mourning for his father he went beyond the prescribed rites, and thereby became known while still young.

sentences.zh: 家世儉約，居甚貧寠。

translations.literal: His family for generations was frugal; their dwelling was very poor and cramped.
translations.idiomatic: His family had been frugal for generations, and they lived in great poverty.

sentences.zh: 有弟五人，皆幼弱。

translations.literal: He had five younger brothers, all young and weak.
translations.idiomatic: He had five younger brothers, all still small.

sentences.zh: 不害事老母，養小弟，勤劇無所不至，士大夫以篤行稱之。

translations.literal: Buhai served his aged mother and raised his younger brothers, toiling at every task without exception; scholar-officials praised him for his earnest conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Buhai cared for his aged mother and raised his younger brothers, laboring at every task without stint. Scholar-officials praised him for his steadfast devotion.

sentences.zh: 年十七，仕梁為廷尉平，長於政事，兼飾以儒術，名法有輕重不便者，輒上書言之，多見納用。

translations.literal: At seventeen he entered service under Liang as assistant judge of the Court of Judicial Review, excelled in administrative affairs, and additionally adorned himself with Confucian learning; where names and laws had weights and inconveniences, he would memorialize about them, and many were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen he entered Liang service as assistant judge of the Court of Judicial Review. He excelled at administration and grounded his work in Confucian learning. When he found flaws in the penal code he memorialized the throne, and many of his proposals were adopted.

sentences.zh: 大同五年，兼東宮通事舍人。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Datong he served concurrently as Attendant for General Affairs in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Datong he served concurrently as Attendant for General Affairs in the Crown Prince's household.

sentences.zh: 時朝政多委東宮，不害與舍人庾肩吾直日奏事，梁武帝嘗謂肩吾曰：「卿是文學之士，吏事非卿所長，何不使殷不害來邪？

translations.literal: At that time much of court governance was entrusted to the Eastern Palace; Buhai and Attendant Yu Jianwu were on duty presenting affairs. Emperor Wu of Liang once said to Jianwu: "You are a man of literary learning—administrative matters are not your strength. Why not have Yin Buhai come instead?"
translations.idiomatic: At that time much of the court's business was handled through the Crown Prince's household. Buhai and Attendant Yu Jianwu were on duty presenting memorials. Emperor Wu once said to Jianwu, "You are a literary man. Administrative work is not your strength. Why not send Yin Buhai instead?"

sentences.zh: 」其見知如此。

translations.literal: " Thus was he recognized.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 簡文以不害善事親，賜其母蔡氏錦裙襦氈席被褥，單復畢備。

translations.literal: Emperor Jianwen, because Buhai served his parents well, bestowed on his mother Lady Cai brocade skirts and jackets, felt mats, bedding, and quilts—both light and heavy coverings complete.
translations.idiomatic: Because Buhai cared devotedly for his parents, Emperor Jianwen bestowed on his mother Lady Cai brocade skirts and jackets, felt mats, bedding, and quilts of every weight.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，不害從簡文入台。

translations.literal: During the rebellion of Hou Jing, Buhai followed Emperor Jianwen into the palace compound.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion, Buhai followed Emperor Jianwen into the palace compound.

sentences.zh: 及台城陷，簡文在中書省，景帶甲將兵，入朝陛見，過謁簡文，衝突左右，甚不遜，侍衛者莫不驚恐辟易，唯不害與中庶子徐摛侍側不動。

translations.literal: When Taicheng fell, Emperor Jianwen was in the Secretariat; Jing, armored and leading troops, entered the court for audience at the steps, passed to pay respects to Emperor Jianwen, and charged through those at his side with great insolence. The guards all were startled and terrified and shrank back—only Buhai and Palace Mentor Xu Chi stood at his side unmoved.
translations.idiomatic: When Taicheng fell, Emperor Jianwen was in the Secretariat. Hou Jing, armored and at the head of his troops, entered the palace for audience, then went to pay his respects to the emperor, shoving aside those around him with shocking insolence. Every guard was terrified and shrank back—only Buhai and Palace Mentor Xu Chi stood at the emperor's side without moving.

sentences.zh: 簡文為景所幽，遣人請不害與居處，景許之，不害供侍益謹。

translations.literal: Emperor Jianwen was confined by Jing; he sent someone to request that Buhai live with him. Jing consented, and Buhai served and attended with ever greater diligence.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jianwen was confined by Hou Jing, he asked that Buhai be allowed to stay with him. Jing agreed, and Buhai served him with redoubled care.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝立，以不害為中書郎，兼廷尉卿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan of Liang was established, he appointed Buhai Gentleman of the Secretariat and concurrently Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan of Liang took the throne, he appointed Buhai Gentleman of the Secretariat and concurrently Director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 魏平江陵，失母所在。

translations.literal: When Wei pacified Jiangling, he lost track of where his mother was.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Wei captured Jiangling, he lost track of his mother.

sentences.zh: 時甚寒雪，凍死者填滿溝壑。

translations.literal: At the time snow was bitterly cold; the frozen dead filled ditches and ravines.
translations.idiomatic: Snow lay deep and the cold was fierce. The frozen dead filled every ditch and ravine.

sentences.zh: 不害行哭尋求，聲不暫輟。

translations.literal: Buhai walked weeping as he searched; his voice did not cease for a moment.
translations.idiomatic: Buhai walked the streets weeping as he searched, never pausing in his cries.

sentences.zh: 遇見死人溝中，即投身捧視，舉體凍僵，水漿不入口者七日，始得母屍。

translations.literal: Whenever he came upon a corpse in a ditch he would throw himself forward and lift it to look; his whole body frozen stiff, he took neither water nor food for seven days before he at last found his mother's corpse.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he found a corpse in a ditch he would throw himself forward to examine it. His whole body froze stiff. For seven days he took neither water nor food before he at last found his mother's body.

sentences.zh: 憑屍而哭，每舉音輒氣絕，行路皆為流涕。

translations.literal: Leaning on the corpse he wept; each time he raised his voice his breath stopped. Passersby all wept for him.
translations.idiomatic: He leaned on the body and wept until he lost consciousness with every cry. Passersby wept at the sight.

sentences.zh: 即江陵權殯，與王褒、庾信俱入長安。

translations.literal: He provisionally interred her at Jiangling, then entered Chang'an together with Wang Xiang and Yu Xin.
translations.idiomatic: He gave her provisional burial at Jiangling, then was taken to Chang'an together with Wang Xiang and Yu Xin.

sentences.zh: 自是蔬食布衣，枯槁骨立，見者莫不哀之。

translations.literal: From then on he ate vegetables and wore plain cloth; withered and only bones standing, all who saw him were moved to pity.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he ate only vegetables and wore plain cloth. Wasted to skin and bone, he moved all who saw him to pity.

sentences.zh: 不佞字季卿，少立名節，居父喪以至孝稱。

translations.literal: Buniu, courtesy name Jiqing, established reputation and integrity while young; in mourning for his father he was famed for utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Buniu, courtesy name Jiqing, established his reputation for integrity while still young and was known for exceptional filial devotion during his father's mourning.

sentences.zh: 好讀書，尤長吏術。

translations.literal: He loved reading books and was especially skilled in the methods of administration.
translations.idiomatic: He loved reading and was especially skilled in administrative affairs.

sentences.zh: 梁承聖初，為武康令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chengsheng of Liang, he served as Magistrate of Wukang.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Chengsheng era he served as magistrate of Wukang.

sentences.zh: 時兵荒饑饉，百姓流移，不佞循撫招集，繈負至者以千數。

translations.literal: At the time there were war, desolation, and famine; the people drifted in displacement. Buniu guided, comforted, and gathered them, and those who came carrying infants on their backs numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: War, famine, and displacement ravaged the region. Buniu guided and comforted the people and gathered them in; refugees carrying infants on their backs came by the thousands.

sentences.zh: 會魏克江陵，而母卒，道路隔絕，久不得奔赴。

translations.literal: It happened that Wei captured Jiangling and his mother died; roads were cut off, and for a long time he could not rush to attend.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Wei captured Jiangling his mother died. The roads were cut off and for a long time he could not reach her.

sentences.zh: 四載之中，晝夜號泣，居處飲食，常為居喪之禮。

translations.literal: Within four years he wept day and night; in dwelling, conduct, eating, and drinking he constantly observed the rites of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: For four years he wept day and night. In his daily life, eating and drinking, he observed every rite of mourning.

sentences.zh: 陳武帝受禪，除婁令。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Chen received the abdication, Buniu was appointed Magistrate of Lou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Chen took the throne, Buniu was appointed magistrate of Lou.

sentences.zh: 至是第四兄不齊始於江陵迎母喪柩歸葬。

translations.literal: At this point his fourth elder brother Buqi at last went from Jiangling to bring their mother's coffin home for burial.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did his fourth elder brother Buqi bring their mother's coffin back from Jiangling for burial.

sentences.zh: 不佞居處之節，如始聞問，若此者又三年。

translations.literal: Buniu's conduct in daily life was as when he first heard the news; thus it continued for another three years.
translations.idiomatic: Buniu continued to live as though he had just received word of her death—and did so for another three years.

sentences.zh: 身自負土，手植松柏，每歲時伏臘，必三日不食。

translations.literal: He personally carried earth on his back and planted pines and cypresses with his own hands; each year at the seasonal sacrifices of Fuxi and La, he always went three days without eating.
translations.idiomatic: He carried earth for the grave himself and planted pines and cypresses with his own hands. At every seasonal sacrifice he fasted for three days.

sentences.zh: 司馬暠字文升，河內溫人也。

translations.literal: Sima Hao, style name Wensheng, was a man of Wen in Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Hao, courtesy name Wensheng, was a native of Wen in Henei.

sentences.zh: 高祖柔之，晉侍中，以南頓王孫紹齊文獻王攸後。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Rouzhi was a Jin Attendant-in-Ordinary; as grandson of the Prince of Nandun he continued the line of Qi Prince Wenxian Wang You.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Rouzhi had been a Jin Attendant-in-Ordinary; as a descendant of the Prince of Nandun he carried on the line of Prince Wenxian of Qi, Wang You.

sentences.zh: 父子產，即梁武帝之外兄也，位岳陽太守。

translations.literal: His father Zichan was none other than Emperor Wu of Liang's elder cousin by marriage, and held the post of Administrator of Yueyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zichan was Emperor Wu of Liang's elder cousin by marriage and served as Administrator of Yueyang.

sentences.zh: 暠幼聰警，有至性。

translations.literal: Hao from youth was clever and alert, with utmost nature.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood Hao was quick-witted and possessed a deeply sincere nature.

sentences.zh: 年十二，丁內艱，哀慕過禮，水漿不入口，殆經一旬。

translations.literal: At twelve he suffered bereavement for his mother, grieving beyond the rites, taking no food or drink for nearly ten days.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he lost his mother and mourned beyond the prescribed rites, taking no food or drink for nearly ten days.

sentences.zh: 每號慟，必至悶絕，父每喻之，令進粥，然猶毀瘠骨立。

translations.literal: Each time he wailed he would fall unconscious; his father repeatedly admonished him and had him take gruel, yet he was still wasted to skin and bone.
translations.idiomatic: Each fit of weeping left him unconscious. His father urged him again and again to take gruel, yet he remained wasted to skin and bone.

sentences.zh: 服闋，以姻戚子弟入問訊，梁武帝見其羸疾，歎息久之。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he entered as a kinsman youth to pay respects; Emperor Wu of Liang saw how frail and ill he was and sighed for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he paid court as a kinsman youth. Emperor Wu saw how frail he was and sighed at length.

sentences.zh: 字其小字謂其父曰：「昨見羅兒面顏憔悴，使人惻然，便是不墜家風，為有子矣。

translations.literal: He used his pet name and said to his father: "Yesterday I saw Luor's face haggard and wan, which moves one to pity—this shows he does not fail the family tradition; he is truly a son.
translations.idiomatic: Using the boy's pet name he told his father, "Yesterday I saw Luor's face drawn and haggard—it wrings the heart. He has not failed the family tradition; you have a true son.

sentences.zh: 」後累遷正員郎。

translations.literal: " Later he was repeatedly promoted to Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: " He was later promoted to Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 丁父艱，哀毀愈甚，廬於墓側，日進薄麥粥一升。

translations.literal: When his father died his grief and devastation grew still worse; he built a hut beside the tomb and each day took only one sheng of thin wheat gruel.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died his grief deepened. He built a mourning hut beside the tomb and ate only a sheng of thin wheat gruel each day.

sentences.zh: 墓在新林，連接山阜，舊多猛獸，暠結廬數載，豺狼絕跡。

translations.literal: The tomb was at Xinlin, linked to mountain ridges where fierce beasts had long been numerous; Hao built his hut for several years, and wolves and jackals vanished without trace.
translations.idiomatic: The tomb lay at Xinlin among hills once thick with wild beasts. After Hao kept his hut there for years, wolves and jackals vanished from the place.

sentences.zh: 常有兩鳩棲宿廬所，馴狎異常。

translations.literal: Two turtledoves constantly roosted at his hut, tame beyond the ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Two turtledoves constantly roosted at his hut, unusually tame.

sentences.zh: 承聖中，除太子庶子。

translations.literal: During the Chengsheng era he was appointed Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chengsheng era he was appointed Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 魏克江陵，隨例入長安。

translations.literal: When Wei captured Jiangling he followed the usual course and entered Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When the Northern Wei took Jiangling he was taken to Chang'an like the rest.

sentences.zh: 而梁宗屠戮，太子殯瘞失所，及周受禪，暠以宮臣，乃抗表求還江陵改葬，辭甚酸切。

translations.literal: But the Liang imperial clan had been slaughtered and the crown prince's burial was misplaced; when Zhou received the mandate Hao, as a former palace official, submitted a bold memorial asking to return to Jiangling for reburial, his words exceedingly bitter and urgent.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang imperial house had been slaughtered and the crown prince's burial was lost. When the Zhou took power, Hao as a former palace official submitted a bold memorial begging to return to Jiangling for a proper reburial, his words bitter and urgent.

sentences.zh: 周朝優詔答之，即敕荊州以禮安厝。

translations.literal: The Zhou court answered with a gracious edict and immediately ordered Jingzhou to lay the remains to rest according to rites.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou court replied with a gracious edict and ordered Jingzhou to bury the prince with full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 陳太建八年，自周還，宣帝特降殊禮。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Chen's Taijian era he returned from Zhou; Emperor Xuan specially granted him exceptional honors.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Taijian he returned from the north; Emperor Xuan granted him exceptional honors.

sentences.zh: 歷位通直散騎常侍、太中大夫，卒。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Master of Palace Counsel, then died.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Master of Palace Counsel, then died.

sentences.zh: 有集十卷。

translations.literal: He left a collected works in ten juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collected works in ten juan.

sentences.zh: 子延義字希忠，少沈敏好學。

translations.literal: His son Yanyi, style name Xizhong, from youth was deep, keen, and fond of learning.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yanyi, courtesy name Xizhong, was from youth thoughtful, keen, and devoted to learning.

sentences.zh: 初隨父入關，丁母憂，喪過於禮。

translations.literal: At first he followed his father into the passes; when his mother died his mourning exceeded the rites.
translations.idiomatic: He first followed his father into the north. When his mother died he mourned beyond the prescribed rites.

sentences.zh: 及暠還都，延義乃躬負靈櫬，晝伏宵行，冒履冰霜，手足皸瘃。

translations.literal: When Hao returned to the capital, Yanyi personally shouldered the coffin, lying low by day and traveling by night, braving frost and ice until his hands and feet were chapped and frostbitten.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao returned to the capital, Yanyi shouldered the coffin himself, hiding by day and traveling by night through frost and ice until his hands and feet were cracked and numb.

sentences.zh: 至都，遂致攣廢，數年乃愈。

translations.literal: On reaching the capital he was stricken with crippling contracture and only after several years recovered.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he reached the capital he was crippled by contracture and did not recover for several years.

sentences.zh: 位司徒從事中郎。

translations.literal: He rose to the post of Attendant Gentleman of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Attendant Gentleman under the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 張昭字德明，吳郡吳人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhao, style name Deming, was a man of Wu in Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhao, courtesy name Deming, was a native of Wu in Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 幼有孝性，父熯常患消渴，嗜鮮魚，昭乃身自結網捕魚，以供朝夕。

translations.literal: From youth he had a filial nature; his father Yan often suffered from wasting thirst and craved fresh fish, so Zhao himself wove nets and caught fish to supply morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he was filial. His father Yan suffered from wasting thirst and craved fresh fish, so Zhao wove nets and caught fish himself for every meal.

sentences.zh: 弟幹字玄明，聰敏好學，亦有至性。

translations.literal: His younger brother Gan, style name Xuanming, was clever and keen, fond of learning, and also had utmost nature.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Gan, courtesy name Xuanming, was clever and studious and equally possessed a deeply sincere nature.

sentences.zh: 及父卒，兄弟並不衣綿帛，不食鹽酢，日唯食一升麥屑粥。

translations.literal: When their father died the brothers both wore no silk or brocade, ate no salt or vinegar, and each day took only one sheng of wheat-bran gruel.
translations.idiomatic: When their father died both brothers wore no silk, took no salt or vinegar, and ate only a sheng of wheat-bran gruel each day.

sentences.zh: 每一感慟，必致歐血，鄰里聞之，皆為涕泣。

translations.literal: Each time grief seized them they would vomit blood; neighbors who heard it all wept.
translations.idiomatic: Each fit of grief brought up blood; neighbors who heard them wept.

sentences.zh: 父服未終，母陸氏又卒，兄弟遂六年哀毀，形容骨立。

translations.literal: Before mourning for their father had ended their mother Lady Lu also died; the brothers then grieved and were devastated for six years until they were skin and bone.
translations.idiomatic: Before their father's mourning had ended their mother Lady Lu died as well. The brothers mourned for six years until they were wasted to skin and bone.

sentences.zh: 家貧，未得大葬，遂布衣蔬食，十有餘年，杜門不出，屏絕人事。

translations.literal: The family was poor and could not afford full burial; they then wore plain cloth and ate vegetables for more than ten years, shutting the gate and not going out, cutting off all human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Too poor for a proper burial, they wore plain cloth and ate only vegetables for more than ten years, never leaving their gate or receiving visitors.

sentences.zh: 時衡陽王伯信臨州，舉幹孝廉，固辭不就。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Hengyang, Boxin, was governing the province and recommended Gan as Filial and Incorrupt; he firmly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Hengyang, Boxin, governed the province he recommended Gan as Filial and Incorrupt, but Gan firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 兄弟並因毀成疾，昭一眼失明，幹亦中冷苦癖，年並未五十，終於家，子胤俱絕。

translations.literal: Both brothers fell ill from devastation of mourning; Zhao lost sight in one eye, Gan also suffered from chronic cold and painful colic; neither had reached fifty when they died at home, and their sons and heirs were extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Both brothers fell ill from excessive mourning. Zhao lost sight in one eye; Gan suffered chronic cold and colic. Neither reached fifty when they died at home, and their line ended without heirs.

sentences.zh: 宣帝時，有太原王知玄者，僑居會稽剡縣，居家以孝聞。

translations.literal: During Emperor Xuan's reign there was Wang Zhixuan of Taiyuan, living as a sojourner in Yan County of Kuaiji, known at home for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Xuan's reign there was Wang Zhixuan of Taiyuan, a sojourner in Yan County of Kuaiji, renowned at home for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 及丁父憂，哀毀而卒。

translations.literal: When he suffered bereavement for his father he grieved and was devastated unto death.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he mourned himself to death.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉之，詔改所居青苦裏為孝家裏。

translations.literal: The emperor commended him and issued an edict changing the lane where he had lived, Qingku Li, to Xiaojia Li.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended him and ordered the lane where he had lived, Bitter Suffering Lane, renamed Filial Family Lane.

sentences.zh: 論曰：自澆風一起，人倫毀薄，蓋抑引之教，導俗所先，變裏旌閭，義存勸獎。

translations.literal: The discussion says: From the time the degenerate wind arose, human relations were ruined and thin—for restraining and drawing forth is the teaching that guides custom beforehand; changing lanes and honoring gates and wards preserves the meaning of encouragement and reward.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Once corrupt customs took hold, human bonds grew thin. Teaching that restrains excess and draws virtue forth must lead the way in guiding society; renaming lanes and honoring households at the gate preserves the purpose of encouragement and reward.

sentences.zh: 是以漢世士務修身，故忠孝成俗，至於乘軒服冕，非此莫由。

translations.literal: Therefore in Han times gentlemen devoted themselves to cultivating the person, and loyalty and filial piety became custom; as for riding in carriages and wearing coronets, there was no other path than this.
translations.idiomatic: Thus in Han times gentlemen devoted themselves to self-cultivation, and loyalty and filial piety became the norm. Carriages and court robes came by no other road.

sentences.zh: 晉、宋以來，風衰義缺，刻身厲行，事薄膏腴。

translations.literal: From Jin and Song onward the wind declined and righteousness was lacking; carving the body and steeling conduct became matters thin and meager.
translations.idiomatic: From the Jin and Song dynasties onward customs decayed and righteousness waned; austere self-discipline came to seem a poor substitute for comfort and rank.

sentences.zh: 若使孝立閨庭，忠被史策，多發溝畎之中，非出衣簪之下。

translations.literal: If filial piety is established within the inner court and loyalty recorded in the histories, it mostly springs from ditches and furrows, not from beneath cap and hairpin.
translations.idiomatic: When filial piety flourishes in humble homes and loyalty earns a place in the histories, the examples mostly rise from ditches and furrows, not from beneath official caps and hairpins.

sentences.zh: 以此而言聲教，不亦卿大夫之恥乎。

translations.literal: To speak of sound teaching on this basis—is it not also a shame to ministers and grandees?
translations.idiomatic: Judged by this standard, what does moral instruction say about the great offices—if not that they ought to feel ashamed?
